author: Baron Godfrey Rathbone Benson Charnwood
claims: Abraham Lincoln was elected President of the United States.
On the night of November 6, 1860, Lincoln received election results in a telegraph box in Springfield.
Lincoln was confident of his victory before all election returns were complete.
Lincoln began planning his Cabinet on election night.
Lincoln was elected by a minority of the American people based on popular votes.
Lincoln's votes came exclusively from the Northern states; he carried almost all free states and no others.
For the first time, the united North used its superior numbers to outvote the South.
The election of Lincoln was met with derision in the South.
The Presidential election took place on November 6, 1860.
The President-elect does not enter office for nearly four months after the election.
Secession was carried in South Carolina in December following the election.
